item.title: The center of an associative crossed module
item.description: arXiv:2611.09360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we define a Drinfeld-type center for an associative crossed module and prove that it is canonically the internal category of an explicit crossed module constructed from Mac Lane's bimultiplications. The resulting center carries a canonical multiplicative lifting, which induces a natural strict braiding, establishing its correspondence to a braided crossed module. We also examine the relationship between this center and Huq's categorical center. Finally, we obtain a canonical comparison morphism with Pirashvili's center of Lie crossed modules via the (braided) Liezation functors, which preserves braidings under an injectivity condition.
item.dc:creator: Emzar Khmaladze, Manuel Ladra, David Quiroga, Brais Ramos P\'erez

item.title: Inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals
item.description: arXiv:2611.09415v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inclusions and intersections of products of verbally prime $T$-ideals over a field of characteristic zero. Our main tool is a Vandermonde-type construction of graded polynomials with a uniformly bounded number of variables. Together with a reduction to finite exterior algebras, this construction yields separating polynomials that work uniformly under bounds on Grassmann envelope representations. We prove that, under these bounds, an intersection of $T$-ideals is contained in such a product only if one member is. This proves Berele's Conjecture~3 and, consequently, his Conjecture~1 \cite{Berele2012}. We also characterize inclusions between ordered products by an explicit combinatorial criterion, proving his Conjecture~2 and answering his Question~2 \cite{Berele2012}. These results characterize inclusions between arbitrary intersections of products of nonzero proper verbally prime $T$-ideals and show that every nonzero such intersection has a unique finite irredundant representation. As an application, we characterize finite quivers whose path algebras have the same polynomial identities as some, equivalently every, positive power of their arrow ideals.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Zheng, Shenglin Zhu

item.title: Weighted \texorpdfstring{$\mathcal{O}$}-operators on pre-Leibniz algebras and post-pre-Leibniz structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.09460v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators (also called weighted relative Rota-Baxter operators) on pre-Leibniz algebras. We construct a differential graded Lie algebra whose Maurer-Cartan elements are exactly these operators. This allows us to define their cohomology as that of the induced pre-Leibniz algebra with coefficients in a suitable representation. As an application, we study formal and finite order deformations of these operators. We show that this theory splits the corresponding theory for weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators on Leibniz algebras. Finally, we introduce post-pre-Leibniz algebras as the algebraic structures underlying weighted $\mathcal{O}$-operators on pre-Leibniz algebras.
item.dc:creator: Sami Benabdelhafidh

item.title: An extension of the notion of algebraic entropy
item.description: arXiv:2611.09602v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The definition of algebraic entropy presents a difficulty in the general setting of filtered algebras, which makes it necessary to distinguish between filtered algebras and finitely filtered algebras. While algebraic entropy is well defined in the finitely filtered case, extending this notion to arbitrary filtered algebras is not immediate. To address this issue, we realize a filtered algebra as the limit of a strict direct system of finitely filtered algebras and define its entropy as the supremum of the entropies of the algebras in the system. This extension is consistent with the original definition, when the algebra is finitely filtered, the extended entropy agrees with its algebraic entropy. This new setting allows us to extend the definition of the algebraic entropy to path and Leavitt path algebras of infinite graphs.
item.dc:creator: Dolores Mart\'in Barquero, C\'andido Mart\'in Gonz\'alez, Iv\'an Ruiz Campos

item.title: Topological Mundici Adjunction and Its Applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.09608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a canonical topological lifting of Mundici equivalence, representing every topological MV-algebra as the unit interval of a topological $\ell$-group and extending the correspondence to a categorical adjunction. As applications, we give a direct group-theoretic proof of the equivalence of $T_0$ and $T_{3\frac12}$ and show that every topological MV-algebra is a retral space. We further extend the lifting to topological Riesz MV-algebras and identify the canonical topology with Wiweger's mixed topology under suitable assumptions, recovering the strict topology as a special case. Finally, we obtain a unit-interval formulation of Koopman representations for continuous-time dynamical systems.
item.dc:creator: Yanqiao Jia, Xueting Zhao, Yichuan Yang

item.title: Division ring extensions and a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.09749v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a family of division ring extensions and compute their left and right dimensions. In characteristic zero, we obtain a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture: a hereditary right pure semisimple ring of infinite representation type. For each prime $p\ge3$, we construct in characteristic $p$ a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(p+2)$.
item.dc:creator: A. I. Generalov, A. Tursunbaev

item.title: Deformations and Local Geometry of Lie Triple System Morphisms
item.description: arXiv:2611.09849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, first we study the deformations, stability and rigidity of Lie triple system morphisms by means of higher derived brackets and augmented Yamaguti cohomology. The vanishing of the first cohomology gives formal and local inner rigidity. The vanishing of the second cohomology removes the formal extension obstructions and, in finite dimension over $\mathbb{R}$, gives local smoothness and stability under simultaneous perturbations of the two products. Next, we establish the relationship with Lie algebra homomorphisms in each part of the theory. The universal enveloping Lie algebra identifies a Lie triple morphism with a grading-preserving Lie homomorphism. We obtain the corresponding first cohomology isomorphism, the equivalence of formal and smooth deformations, and a stability result for graded Lie bracket perturbations. For Lie triple products induced by binary Lie brackets, we construct a comparison of differentials and obstruction classes. Under perfectness and a zero-centralizer condition, the local morphism spaces coincide. Finally, we relate triple subsystem graphs to graded Lie subalgebra graphs and compare their normal differentials.
item.dc:creator: Wen Teng, Ripan Saha

item.title: The quaternionic reflection groups with imprimitive complexifications and the finite subgroups of GL(2,C)
item.description: arXiv:2611.08691v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a transparent development of the quaternionic reflection groups which have imprimitive complexifications, including a description of their reflections and the corresponding normal reflection subgroups. They are seen to be of rank one or rank two, and are obtained from minimal complex reflection groups by the addition of one quaternionic reflection and a complex scalar matrix of finite order. In the case of the rank two groups, we use our techniques to consider the broader question of what are the minimal irreducible subgroups of GL(2,C) with a given collineation group. This leads to a complete classification of the finite irreducible subgroups of GL(2,C) in terms of the minimal groups, with the groups giving rise to quaternionic reflection groups located within it.
item.dc:creator: Shayne Waldron

item.title: Centres and semisimple deformations of contraction algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.09220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $A_{\rm{con}}$ be the contraction algebra of a $3$-fold flop of an irreducible curve, with genus-zero Gopakumar-Vafa invariants $n_1, \dots, n_l$. We show that $\prod_j M_j(\mathbb{C})^{n_j}$ is the only semisimple algebra to which $A_{\rm{con}}$ deforms. Hence $A_{\rm{con}}$ encodes its Gopakumar-Vafa invariants intrinsically, answering a question of Wemyss. Hua and Toda showed that this deformation exists, and Jelisiejew and Smoktunowicz proved its uniqueness in types A and D. The key step in our proof is that the centre of $A_{\rm{con}}$ has dimension $n_1 + \dots + n_l$. To prove this, we lift the contraction algebra of the universal flop to the Cartan subalgebra, where it becomes a corner of a deformed preprojective algebra. We show that the universal contraction algebra and its zeroth Hochschild homology are free over a polynomial ring, with presentations whose determinants are products of roots. Pulling these presentations back along the arc that classifies the flop gives the count, and recovers Toda's formula for $\dim A_{\rm{con}}$. We also prove Hua and Toda's flatness conjecture, and determine which Gopakumar-Vafa invariants occur in lengths 3 to 6.
item.dc:creator: Joseph Karmazyn, Shengyong Pan

item.title: Isomorphic classification of the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups $\mathrm{SL}_2$
item.description: arXiv:2611.09369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We classify, up to isomorphism, the coordinate algebras of the two-parameter braided quantum groups SL 2 .
item.dc:creator: Julien Bichon (LMBP), Thi Hoa Emilie Nguyen (LMBP)

item.title: Two-step nilpotent varieties as categories of modules over a square ring
item.description: arXiv:2611.09465v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterise the two-step nilpotent varieties of algebras: the semi-abelian varieties in which all ternary cosmash products vanish. Just as abelian varieties are the categories of modules over a ring, two-step nilpotent varieties are exactly the categories of modules over a square ring in the sense of Baues, Hartl and Pirashvili. We construct the square ring explicitly from the full subcategory on the free algebras on one and two generators, and give complete proofs. As consequences we obtain a description of any two-step nilpotent variety by generators and relations, an intrinsic characterisation in terms of quadratic term operations, and an account of its abelian core and of the lower central series of its objects in terms of the square ring. Along the way, we associate with any commutative ring $R$ a square ring whose modules, the two-step nilpotent $R$-groups, extend Hall's nilpotent $R$-groups of class two from $2$-binomial rings to arbitrary rings of coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Logan Geenis, Manfred Hartl, Tim Van der Linden

item.title: Weakly Unitary Zeon Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.33891v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, zeon matrix groups are discussed for the first time. Extending the concept of unitary complex matrices (i.e., matrices $A$ such that $A^\dagger A=\mI$) to matrices having entries in the complex zeon algebra $\CZ$, a ``zeon dagger'' operator $\zdag$ is defined and used to declare a zeon matrix $\Xi$ to be {\em unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI$. The unitary zeon matrices of order $n$ form a subgroup $\U_n$ of all invertible order-$n$ zeon matrices. A more interesting notion is that of ``weak unitarity'' of a zeon matrix. In particular, a zeon matrix $\Xi$ will be said to be {\em weakly unitary} if $\Xi^\zdag\Xi=\mI+\Gamma$, where $\Gamma$ is a diagonal nilpotent zeon matrix. The weakly unitary matrices of order $n$ form a group $\W_n$, of which $\U_n$ is a subgroup. It is further shown that the exponential of a graph's nilpotent adjacency matrix has a natural orthogonal decomposition into the sum of a weakly unitary zeon matrix and a nilpotent zeon matrix. Eigenvalues of the weakly unitary zeon matrix reveal information about the graph's cycles and paths.
item.dc:creator: G. Stacey Staples

item.title: Semibricks and wide subcategories in extended module categories
item.description: arXiv:2511.08157v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $d\geq 1$, we define semibricks and wide subcategories in the $d$-extended hearts of bounded $t$-structures on a triangulated category. We show that these semibricks are in bijection with finite-length wide subcategories. When the $d$-extended heart is the $d$-extended module category $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}\Lambda$ of a finite-dimensional algebra $\Lambda$ over a field, we define left/right-finite semibricks and left/right-finite wide subcategories in $d\mbox{-}\mathrm{mod}\Lambda$ and show bijections with $(d+1)$-term simple-minded collections, generalising the bijections between $2$-term simple-minded collections, left/right-finite wide subcategories and left/right-finite semibricks in $\mathrm{mod}\Lambda$. We use a relation between semibricks and silting complexes to characterise which mutations of $(d+1)$-term silting complexes are again $(d+1)$-term.
item.dc:creator: Esha Gupta, Yu Zhou

item.title: Actions in varieties of non-associative algebras: a survey
item.description: arXiv:2610.18302v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article surveys the main results on the representability of internal actions in varieties of non-associative algebras over a field. We begin by recalling the general framework of internal actions and split extensions in semi-abelian categories, before specialising to Orzech categories of interest and varieties of non-associative algebras. We discuss action representability, weak action representability, and action accessibility, with emphasis on the relationship between the latter two notions. We then describe the constructions of the universal strict general actor in Orzech categories of interest and the external weak actor in action accessible, operadic varieties of non-associative algebras over a field, as well as their role in the study of weak action representability. We also give a tensor-domain formulation of partial algebras and adapt the construction of the external weak actor to this setting. These notions are illustrated by examples arising from associative, Lie, Leibniz, Jacobi-Jordan, anti-commutative anti-associative, alternative, and $2$-nilpotent algebras. We conclude with a summary of the known results and some open questions for future research.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Mancini

item.title: All totally real abelian number fields of class number one are Euclidean
item.description: arXiv:2610.24900v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It is a famous result of Narkiewicz that there are at most two real quadratic and at most one totally real cubic Galois extensions $K/\mathbb Q$, whose ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ is a unique factorization domain (UFD), but not Euclidean. As predicted by another famous result due to Weinberger, these exceptions should in fact not exist, as their existence would contradict a generalized version of the Riemann hypothesis. Building on recent spectacular progress on the Quasi-Riemann hypothesis for Hecke characters, in this short note we close the above final gap provided by Narkiewicz's result, and show, more generally, that the ring of integers $\mathcal O_K$ of any totally real abelian number field $K$ is a UFD, if and only if it is Euclidean. By referring to an additional announced uniform zero-free half-plane for general Dedekind zeta functions, we also establish the corresponding result for certain explicit new families of non-Galois cubic, quartic and quintic fields of unit rank one or two.
item.dc:creator: Harald Grobner
